scope: External provider evaluation for the platform-neutral ORD-A08 Node staging runtime.

strengths: Git-connected deployments and explicit healthcheck support
Public deployment API with logs, deploy and rollback operations
Low operational surface for a small team
Hobby subscription starts at USD 5 monthly and counts toward resource usage
constraints: No Brazil deployment region in the current official region list
Deployment healthcheck is an activation gate rather than continuous uptime monitoring
A paid Hobby plan is the practical minimum for persistent staging

strengths: Continuous health checks and canary or blue-green deployment strategies
Strong regional placement and runtime control
constraints: Requires more infrastructure ownership through fly.toml, image builds and Machine lifecycle
Credit card is required for new organizations
Rollback and release operation are more CLI and infrastructure intensive

strengths: Native Node web services with Git deployments
Health checks, zero-downtime deploys and instant rollback
Free web service option for experimentation
constraints: No South America region in the current official region list
Free services spin down after fifteen idle minutes and may take about one minute to wake
HTTP request logs and response latency metrics require Pro or higher

strengths: Git-native deployment workflow and strong rollback tooling
Sao Paulo managed infrastructure region on Pro
Zero-configuration Node server deployment introduced in June 2026
constraints: General Node server support is recent compared with the other candidates
Sao Paulo regional compute is available only on Pro
The current Doke runtime and release contract map more directly to a persistent service platform

recommendation.reason: It minimizes operational complexity while supporting the existing Node entrypoint, health contract, Git deployments, server-side variables, logs and deterministic rollback APIs. Latency is acceptable for internal staging and can be reconsidered before production.
